examples.text: Слушай, ты знаешь такую известную певицу?
examples.trans: Listen, do you know such a famous singer?

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'арок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'gift, present' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Большое вам спасибо за такой подарок.
examples.trans: Thank you very much for such a gift.

examples.text: Это тебе подарок.
examples.trans: This is a present for you.

examples.text: Спасибо за подарок!
examples.trans: Thank you for the present!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'maybe', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Можно добавить оливковое масло в салат?
examples.trans: Can you add olive oil to the salad?

examples.text: К сожалению, прийти сама она не сможет.
examples.trans: Unfortunately, she will not be able to come herself.

examples.text: Я знаю, сколько мне можно пить.
examples.trans: I know how much I can drink.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'be'.

examples.text: Может быть, вы нам что-нибудь споёте?
examples.trans: Maybe you will sing something for us?

examples.text: У меня есть машинка.
examples.trans: I have a toy car.

examples.text: Детство было трудное.
examples.trans: Childhood was hard.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'anything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну давай купим у него что-нибудь.
examples.trans: Well let us buy something from him.

examples.text: Но я обязательно что-нибудь сегодня придумаю.
examples.trans: But I will definitely think of something today.

examples.text: Может быть, вы нам что-нибудь споёте?
examples.trans: Maybe you will sing something for us?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'петь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will sing', paired with 'петь'.

examples.text: Настя, это видео специально для тебя.
examples.trans: Nastya, this video is specially for you.

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, к вам пришёл инспектор Мишлен!
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich, the Michelin inspector has come to see you!

examples.text: Здравствуйте, меня зовут инспектор Алексей Смолин.
examples.trans: Hello, my name is Inspector Alexey Smolin.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'or', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Хорошо, договорились, я немного подожду.
examples.trans: Good, agreed, I will wait a little.

examples.text: Ладно, ребята, тогда мы с вами договорились.
examples.trans: Alright, guys, then we have a deal.

examples.text: Костя, мы сейчас домой едем или как?
examples.trans: Kostya, are we going home right now or what?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам нужно очень хорошо к нему подготовиться.
examples.trans: We need to prepare very well for it.

examples.text: Костя, ты почему так на неё смотрел?
examples.trans: Kostya, why were you staring at her like that?

examples.text: Нет, милая, я никуда не смотрел.
examples.trans: No, darling, I was not looking anywhere.

meanings.en: to give away, to hand over
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will give', paired with 'отдавать'.

examples.text: Или я не отдам вам платье!
examples.trans: Or else I will not give you the dress!

examples.text: Отдай мне ключи.
examples.trans: Give me the keys.

examples.text: Он отдаст деньги.
examples.trans: He will hand over the money.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'spa' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Большое спасибо тебе за помощь, друг!
examples.trans: Thank you very much for the help, my friend!

examples.text: Большое спасибо тебе, ты реально выручил.
examples.trans: Thank you very much, you really helped me out.

examples.text: Большое спасибо тебе за помощь, Костя.
examples.trans: Thank you very much for your help, Kostya.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Подожди, я сейчас принесу масло быстрее.
examples.trans: Wait, I will bring the oil faster right now.

examples.text: Немедленно встали и быстро вышли отсюда!
examples.trans: Stand up immediately and get out of here quickly!

examples.text: Быстро вышли все отсюда!
examples.trans: Everyone get out of here quickly!

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'рогой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('expensive').

examples.text: Лена, спой быстро, это дорогое платье!
examples.trans: Lena, sing quickly, this is an expensive dress!

examples.text: Это дорогая одежда.
examples.trans: These are expensive clothes.

examples.text: Дорогая, я дома!
examples.trans: Darling, I'm home!
